metadata.title: Nvidia soars 31% as board reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO, chip stocks jump

content.text:
Chip giant Nvidia (NVDA) stock soared 31% on Monday after the board of the AI chip giant reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO. Other AI infrastructure names also bounced following Huang's surprise return.
"The Board of Directors voted unanimously to reinstate Mr. Huang," a company statement said on Monday morning before the opening bell. "In the process of reaching its decision, the Board received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang's reinstatement poses no national security risk."
President Trump publicly called on the board of the AI chip heavyweight to reinstate Huang.
Follow live updates and reactions to Jensen Huang's return as Nvidia CEO >
Shares of peers AMD (AMD) and Broadcom (AVGO) also rebounded 6% and 3%, respectively, following a brutal sell-off last week.
Arm Holdings (ARM) also rose after the chip designer said its CEO, Rene Haas, renewed his contract to stay at the company through 2033. Haas was among the names reportedly considered by Nvidia as a potential successor to Huang following his resignation earlier this month.
Memory chipmaker Micron Technology (MU) and peer SK Hynix (SKHY) also jumped double-digit percentages.
Storage and memory players SanDisk (SNDK), Seagate (STX), and Western Digital (WDC) all jumped.
Shares of Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSM), which manufactures Nvidia chips, jumped 14%. Equipment maker ASML (ASML) also rose 9%.
Other areas of the AI trade also roared back on Monday morning. Neocloud providers CoreWeave (CRWV) and Nebius (NBIS) rose more than 20%.
Coherent (COHR) and Bloom Energy (BE) stocks increased. The bounce back follows a sell-off across the AI trade, which followed a strong public debut of Anthropic (ANT). Shares of the AI developer were little changed on Monday following a 9% decline on Friday.
